title.en: The author, the setting and the rattrap idea

heading.en: Is the whole world a trap?

hook.en: A poor man who sells little wire rattraps begins to think that the whole world is one big rattrap. Is he right?

objectives.en: Introduce Selma Lagerlöf and the setting of the story
Describe the peddler and his way of life

body.en: Selma Lagerlöf was a Swedish writer and, in 1909, the first woman to win the Nobel Prize in Literature. The Rattrap is set in the iron-mining region of Värmland in Sweden, around Christmas. Like many of her stories, it has the feel of a folk tale and a strong moral message about human goodness.

points.en: First woman to win the Nobel Prize in Literature (1909)
Setting: Värmland, Sweden, iron mines and forges

narration.en: Selma Lagerlöf was a Swedish writer and, in 1909, the first woman to win the Nobel Prize in Literature. The Rattrap is set in the iron-mining region of Värmland in Sweden, around Christmas. Like many of her stories, it has the feel of a folk tale and a strong moral message about human goodness.
Let us draw the peddler's big idea: the world as a rattrap.

say.en: At the centre is the peddler's idea: the world itself is a rattrap.
Riches are the bait. Money tempts us.
Food, shelter and clothing are bait too.
The joys and pleasures of life are also bait.
Once we take the bait, the trap snaps shut.
Later, after his theft, the peddler finds himself trapped.
In the end, only kindness and trust set him free.

body.en: The peddler makes small wire rattraps from materials he begs from shops and farms, and he sells them. When that does not earn enough, he begs or steals a little. Lonely and poor, he comes to see the world as a rattrap: it sets out riches, joys, food and shelter as bait, and once people take the bait, they are trapped.

points.en: A poor, lonely vagabond who sells rattraps
Begs and steals small things to survive
Metaphor: the world is a rattrap
Bait: riches, joys, shelter, food and clothing

problem.en: Why did the peddler think the world was a rattrap?

steps.en: Give his idea: the world offers bait such as riches, joys, food and shelter.
Explain the trap: those who take the bait get caught.
Link to his life: his own poverty and loneliness made him bitter.

answer.en: The peddler felt the world was like a rattrap: it tempts people with bait such as riches, joys, food and shelter, and those who reach for it are caught. His poverty and loneliness made the idea attractive to him.
